title: Michigan's Most Haunted: Inside Lansing's Voodoo's World of Oddtiques
excerpt: Voodoo’s World of Oddtiques in Lansing’s REO Town features antiques, consignment pieces and a museum dedicated to paranormal and mortuary science.
content:
LANSING, Mich. (News 10) - Voodoo’s World of Oddtiques in Lansing’s REO Town features antiques, consignment pieces and a museum dedicated to paranormal and mortuary science.

Co-owner Jennifer Harris and her husband have collected unusual items for more than 30 years. “It’s just been a passion our whole life,” Harris said. “So we decided why not bring it to the community.”

The store’s shelves include antique medical equipment, religious antiques and consignment pieces. Harris said items come from estate sales, consignors nationwide and homeowners clearing out family heirlooms. Many are one of a kind and may not be available again.

A museum behind the store

About three years ago, the couple opened the Other Side Paranormal and Mortuary Science Museum behind the store after noticing customers treating the shop like an exhibit, Harris said. Her husband led tours for the first three years, and Harris has recently begun giving them.

The museum features Voodoo traditions, funeral home artifacts and paranormal history. Guests can bring equipment to test what Harris describes as unexplained phenomena. “We never say anything’s haunted,” she said. “We leave that up to the person that comes in and the experiences that they have within the museum.”

Harris said the storefront draws visitors throughout the year, including during its Mardi Gras and holiday Krampus celebrations.
